event.summary: Updated reboot notice assertion matches the shipped interruption contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. Original considered consequence preserved: naming updates as well as reboots might weaken or misstate the simulated reboot test. TLDR: the changed assertion still distinguishes the required interruption sentence and is followed by independent state and terminal-absence oracles. Synthesis source checks: terminal-multihost.spec.ts:3564-3580 waits for the helm to observe this identified session live before reboot; 3606-3615 stops the owned supervisor, checks stop-terminal-hosts exit status zero, writes a fresh boot identity and restores the same stack; 3656-3663 opens the identified row, waits for its reveal and fake-agent output, then runs that reboot. Thus the fixture does not establish interruption merely by displaying the same text the assertion expects. Lines 3668-3679 still reject a live terminal, reconnect placeholder or non-Interrupted status immediately and after a finite observation window. session_view.rs:3876-3905 emits the exact common sentence prefix the new assertion requires. SPEC.md:3531-3535 says exactly 'Opening an interrupted session shows a centered neutral card in the empty terminal area explaining that a host reboot or a Farhelm update ended the agent and that it needs an intentional restart.' Suggested bucket: other (test correctness). Confidence: confirmed source and contract analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: the assertion change remains sensitive to missing/wrong interruption text, and the unchanged independent state/absence checks reject a different lifecycle outcome; specification expressly requires the new wording. Proposed only, not independently accepted. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no for this one-line test-assertion candidate. Caveats: the host-only reboot fixture is not an old-terminal retirement fixture and does not prove warning delivery, retirement cleanup or confirmation targeting during an update. The known retirement/duplicate-agent consequences supplied by the caller retain that neighbouring-group provenance; this assertion neither introduces them nor supplies a distinct route to them. Endpoint observations do not rule out every transient remount, as the test's own comment states.

event.summary: Removed xterm-specific flood assertions do not apply to the host-terminal browser stack
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: considered whether deleting whole-byte-stream verification, xterm pause/resume and paused-remount tests removes the corresponding grid-terminal behavior checks; no concrete regression established. Details: the removed cases were tagged OLD_TERMINAL_TAG and patched Terminal.prototype.write, raw byte socket input, and __farhelmTest's xterm counters. At this revision e2e/playwright.config.ts:1-4,109-114 runs a single host-terminal stack for each discovered spec and engine. SPEC_impl.md, The grid client (1948-2014), states exactly 'The client sends no flow-control pause or resume: it applies every message as it arrives, applying a large history in slices between frames so that the screen stays usable, and the helm pauses a grid stream on its own queue instead.' Grid stream frames are screen state and history, not a lossless copy of all producer bytes. e2e/tests/grid-flood.spec.ts:155-212 exercises the real stack and requires exactly the retained 12,000 history lines plus screen records, consecutive to the final marker. e2e/grid-client/grid-attach.spec.ts:1162-1175 checks that a stalled grid notice plus socket close retains the reason without reconnecting, and 1177-1192 checks recovery builds a fresh live grid. The removed same-realm counter assertions describe xterm-specific state that this grid does not hold. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage). Confidence: confirmed through source and contract analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: mechanisms differ as specified, and retained grid checks cover the corresponding content and client-lifecycle contract; no specific invalid surviving oracle or product defect identified. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no; this candidate concerns automated test coverage only, without an established shipped loss-of-work route. Caveat: this does not claim the remaining grid test proves every transient screen or all old-terminal paths; grid screens may be skipped by contract, and old-terminal test removal is intentional in the assigned change. The separate relay and supervisor tests cited by the deleted comments still need source verification before completing this pass.

event.summary: Removed xterm-specific flood assertions do not apply to the host-terminal browser stack
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: considered whether deleting whole-byte-stream verification, xterm pause/resume, stalled-viewer and paused-remount tests removes the corresponding grid-terminal behavior checks; no concrete regression established. Details: removed tests are OLD_TERMINAL_TAG cases built around Terminal.prototype.write and xterm counters. e2e/playwright.config.ts:1-4,109-114 runs host-terminal stacks for all discovered specs in both engines. SPEC_impl.md, The grid client (1948-2014), says exactly 'The client sends no flow-control pause or resume: it applies every message as it arrives, applying a large history in slices between frames so that the screen stays usable, and the helm pauses a grid stream on its own queue instead.' e2e/tests/grid-flood.spec.ts:155-212 requires the exact consecutive retained history and screen records at the end of a real-stack flood. e2e/grid-client/grid-attach.spec.ts:1162-1192 checks a stall notice plus close does not reconnect and that recovery creates a fresh live grid. Follow-up source checks completed: crates/farhelm-helm/src/terminal.rs:1655-1815 verifies teardown while the browser is unread, with the grid pause observed before injected stalled detach; 2455-2640 verifies actual helm pause and resume, whole numbered frames in order, and that browser flow controls cannot override grid flow. crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/grid_stream/tests.rs:472-585 pins withheld paused output, lossless appended history, a full writer queue, and reset to retained history after eviction; 770-797 pins pause expiry to ForwarderEnd::Stalled, and 799-835 pins input failure while paused. Thus the replacement's separate layers have relevant assertions rather than only comments claiming coverage. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage). Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: xterm counter oracles do not apply to the specified grid mechanism, and retained source contains distinct content, flow-control, expiry, teardown and recovery oracles; no specific invalid surviving oracle or product defect identified. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no; this concerns removed automated coverage, with no established shipped loss-of-work route. Caveats: these tests do not prove every transient screen, all old-terminal paths, or a real browser's full sixty-second timeout in one end-to-end run. Screen skipping is explicitly allowed by SPEC.md, Terminal experience: 'a viewer that falls behind is sent the screen as it is when it can take more, skipping the screens in between, while every line that entered the scrollback meanwhile is still sent, appended.' The assigned removal intentionally retires old-terminal-only browser cases; this record does not claim general exhaustive coverage.

event.summary: Old-terminal flood and paused-remount checks disappear before retirement
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: sessions still using old terminals lose their real-browser checks for lossless flood delivery, observed pause/resume, stall handling and clean state after leaving a paused attachment. This is a historical regression-test coverage loss, not a demonstrated current production failure. Details: deleted parent terminal-flood.spec.ts:671-739 requires all 800,000 records exactly once/in order plus observed pauseCount>=1 and matching resumeCount, independently of the retained tail. Its stalled-viewer case at :780-937 forces an actual xterm watermark pause, requires the roughly sixty-second interval, visible stalled reason and no automatic recovery, then reattaches. Its same-realm case :987-1092 proves the old mount still paused, restores the shared prototype without releasing that mount, drains the producer off-screen, switches away/back without reloading the realm, and requires no inherited pause or bare resume on the replay-only mount. At the reviewed commit SPEC_impl.md:2294-2311 says the supervisor still adopts and serves an earlier tmux server, and :2956-2978 preserves old agents/tabs and old-terminal support. terminal.js:4712-4753,5335-5371 still implements the per-mount pendingWrite/paused/write-completion watermark mechanism. Competing regressions these deleted assertions distinguish include dropping an earlier flood batch while preserving the final retained tail, disabling watermark accounting while accepting all output, or moving paused/pendingWrite state to page scope so a new attachment inherits a prior pause. No mutation/reproduction was run. Retained-test checks: targeted pinned-tree searches across e2e, Rust end-to-end tests, helm and supervisor source for flood verifier, gated flood, pause counters, watermark, paused-remount and reset-flow witnesses find only the grid flood and a healthy remount hook assertion. terminal.spec.ts:535-577 asserts zeroed hook state but its host-only fixture never enters a byte-stream watermark pause; it cannot exercise inheriting an actually paused old mount. helm terminal.rs:1418-1463 injects pause/resume JSON into a scripted peer and verifies forwarding, not browser counter transitions or whole live old-terminal delivery. The previously read retained grid-flood, grid-attach, grid-stream and relay tests are useful but run different mechanisms and do not replace these old-page oracles. Suggested bucket: other, established harm is regression coverage in maintainer tooling. Confidence: confirmed source/contract analysis only. proposed_drop: false; prior proposals based on no functional regression, grid tests, fixture portability or later retirement are withdrawn, while their original text remains in prior c2 events. possible_cover: supplied g176/c2 is the distinct late-replay-write completion boundary, and g176/c3 is simultaneous sibling isolation; retain provenance without claiming this is their same witness. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from deleting a test alone; possible bugs named above are sensitivity examples, not alleged shipped failures. Later disposition: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 retires old terminals at startup, and f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e removes the byte renderer/writeBytes. That makes the old-specific checks obsolete later, not at 647f0227. Historical fix direction: retain these assertions through an adopted-old fixture until retirement, or remove them together with their consumer. Do not restore a retired renderer on the pinned tip merely to run them. Original consequence preserved: lost whole-stream, flow/stall and paused-remount regression checks. No prohibited coverage sources searched and no runtime execution.

event.summary: Old-terminal large-message acceptance loses its regression check
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. The recorded revision still serves adopted old terminals (SPEC_impl.md:2294-2311,2956-2978), and helm terminal.rs:539-554 expressly retains an 8 MiB message/frame cap because old xterm sends whole pastes as one message; :889-891 dispatches byte streams through the old chunked send_input path. Retained checks actually inspected: terminal.rs:1623-1652 tests rejection at TERM_WS_MAX_MESSAGE+1, using the current constant, so it still passes if the constant is wrongly reduced; :2238-2356 accepts one grid message of exactly 64 KiB and :2372 onward checks oversized-grid refusal. terminal.rs:1271-1355's 8 MiB input is sent directly through SupervisorClient, bypassing WebSocket admission; it checks bounded detach, not socket acceptance or post-send receiver liveness.
